title: 19th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 34 members present, 2 on leave and 10 on official travel. Members debated a motion from Dr. Ahmed Shamheed asking Parliament's view on the higher commercial electricity and water rates paid by small and mid-sized businesses outside Malé: members from both the opposition and the government side backed equal rates, while others argued that costs differ by island and that the services are already subsidised. After a 30-minute recess (10:30 to 11:01) members began debating a government bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 2020/8), including a longer deadline to 2027 for finishing island water and sewerage works. No votes were reported in this part, and the bill debate was still under way when it ends. Members continued debating the bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 8/2020), which moves the legal deadline for providing water and sewerage services to every inhabited island to the end of 2027. Most speakers backed the amendment, and the debate was split along government and opposition lines over who was to blame for stalled or unfinished island projects, with several members raising costs, contractors and delays in their own constituencies. The chair said more members still wanted to speak, so debate on the bill was not finished and will continue at a later sitting; the sitting then closed. The text is partly garbled, and the opening lines belong to a speaker whose header is in part 1.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 34 present, 2 on leave, 10 on official travel

items.title: Motion (Rule 189) by Dr. Ahmed Shamheed on the higher commercial electricity and water rates paid by businesses outside Malé
items.outcome: debated; recess called at 10:30; no vote in this part

items.title: Government bill (sponsored by Dhidhdhoo member Abdul Latheef Mohamed) to amend the Water and Sewerage Act, Law 2020/8
items.outcome: debate started after the recess; continues into part 2

items.title: Bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 8/2020): general debate continued, deadline moved to 2027
items.outcome: debated, not concluded; to resume at a later sitting

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Spoke on discrimination in services, saying Laamu islands such as Hithadhoo and Kunahandhoo have stalled water and sewerage works.
Urged action rather than speeches and said Kunahandhoo residents are in poor condition because of water and sewerage problems.
Was reminded by the chair that debating yesterday's bill is not allowed under today's motion.
Supported the amendment but worried about its delivery; said work in Laamu islands such as Hithadhoo and Kunahandhoo had barely started and urged the government to begin.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported the motion and said island guesthouses and businesses pay large power bills; urged all parties to work on a fix.
Questioned spending priorities, citing a drone show and about 800 added FENAKA staff, while Addu and Malé had power cuts.
Said household and business bills are rising and Malé residents sat in blackouts for hours.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Strongly supported the amendment and its rules on contractor companies; said sewerage work in Nilandhoo has dragged on for years.
Questioned the quoted price for the Kondey project and asked for a Finance Committee review.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Moved the Rule 189 motion asking members' views on small and mid-sized businesses outside Malé paying far higher commercial water and power rates.
Cited atoll tariffs tens of percent above Greater Malé and argued the gap conflicts with the Constitution's equal-treatment provisions.
Said the change moves the finish date from 2025 to 2027; criticised the transfer of projects to MWSC and what he saw as low spending of budgeted water, sewerage and housing money.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Called the motion important and said island guesthouses and small shops pay far more than Malé businesses, so the gap needs fixing.
On the water bill, reviewed how many islands got water and sewerage under the previous government and questioned the 2027 extension.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Said his main concern is service access, noting Thulhaadhoo, Fulhadhoo, Fehendhoo and Goidhoo lack reliable power, water, sewerage and health services.
Hoped the government would finish water and sewerage works on two of those islands within three months.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Supported the motion, citing the Constitution's duty to provide basic services without discrimination.
Said guesthouses and other businesses are growing in Thoddoo and high rates hurt them; urged the government to change the rates.
Supported the amendment in general and asked for criteria to be included in the amendment to Article 15; said many islands were largely complete when the last government ended.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: On the motion, said larger priorities are overlooked, noting about MVR 123 billion spent over 17 years while services lag, and cited corruption in past projects.
On the water bill, said basic services were not delivered in 17 years of the Constitution, blamed misused funds and urged accountability.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Argued earlier water and sewerage projects cost far more than comparable work and left large debts; spoke about corruption in basic services; was reminded by the chair to name members properly.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Supported the motion and urged members of all parties to work together on a solution, noting the utility regulator's mandate.
Raised Addu power cuts, saying the problem remains unresolved two years into the government and spare parts have not arrived.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Said the motion is worded to confuse the public and that equal treatment does not mean identical rates because land, fuel and service costs differ.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Argued water and power are already subsidised, with about MVR 55 million paid monthly to STO, and Greater Malé's larger customer base lowers costs.
Said Addu's power problems and the Auditor General's report on the Addu engine house should be examined.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked the government for a quick fix to Addu power cuts and said he supports lower, uniform tariffs.
Said the government reduced electricity unit rates last month and contrasted this with the opposition's record while in government.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the motion, saying businesses should have equal footing wherever they operate since taxes such as GST are the same everywhere.
Said late government payments to contractors and suppliers hurt businesses and called for quick action.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the motion and credited the President with narrowing essential-service prices earlier this year.
Said both utilities are state-owned, so equal rates should be funded by the government, and criticised infrastructure shortfalls despite large spending.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Cited the Constitution's rights chapter and asked why rate gaps were left uncorrected by earlier governments.
Credited the President's approach and said the gap went unaddressed during the previous ten-year MDP period.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Fully supported the motion and regretted that some members defend different charges for essential services between Malé and islands.
Criticised the government's borrowing, saying national debt reached about MVR 123 billion, and raised FENAKA's debt.
Said tariffs outside Malé should match Malé's, noting a targeted subsidy listed in the budget has not been implemented.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said the motion looks like an attempt to gain politically and noted tariffs differ between cities worldwide.
Argued a single national rate would need heavy subsidy and could threaten the utility companies; called for a master plan.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported one national rate for electricity and water, saying atoll businesses and households pay more than Malé.
Said the digital-meter rollout under the previous government did not lower bills and backed more solar generation.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Said the motion is politically motivated and that equipment replaced under the previous government was taken without compensating residents.
Said Madaveli still has outages but equipment is now being sent through FENAKA to fix them.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to what he called false claims about FENAKA staffing.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the water and sewerage amendments and said he would back government bills that benefit residents.
Said Lhohi's water and sewerage work is about 85 percent done and being handed to FENAKA; Velidhoo and Fodhdhoo works are finished.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the 2020 law gave five years to finish the work and the amendment moves that deadline, preferring completion by 2026.
Described Nellaidhoo's sewerage work as unfinished and Vaikaradhoo's as complete, and raised ministers attending Parliament over delays.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the amendment mainly extends the government's own deadline and doubted any date would be met; cited unfinished Addu City services and a promised bridge not yet started.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Criticised ribbon-cutting on projects and a land-allocation bill the President returned; said he could not support the amendment; noted sewerage gaps in Hulhumale' Phase 3, Gulhifalhu and Giraavaru.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Thanked the sponsor and called Article 8(a) the key change; said Hinnavaru residents lack services and expects work to start late this year.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill as a basic-service guarantee; reviewed 2018-2019 project awards and cancellations and the share of islands served by 2013 and by 2023.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Thanked the sponsor; said Gemanafushi sewerage was left unfinished and contractors were struggling financially; said the government will redo and complete the work.

decisions: The chair told members that yesterday's bill could not be debated under the day's motion and asked them to stay on the motion.
The Speaker called a 30-minute recess at 10:30; the sitting resumed at 11:01.
Debate on the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 8/2020) amendment bill was not concluded because more members wished to speak; it will continue at a later sitting.
The chair announced committee meetings for the day: Human Rights and Gender Committee at 10:00 and Economic Committee at 11:00.
